React Compiler: from source policy to safe memoization

A source-backed review of the complete compiler import, with 12 deep-dive chapters and explicit boundaries for tests, runtime compatibility, playground and Rust WIP.

Overview · Overview

Purpose

Review the 3,669-file import by following its semantic boundaries: eligibility and failure policy; HIR/SSA and effect inference; React-rule validation; scope/dependency safety; cache codegen and native/compat runtime; diagnostic consumers and behavioral test harness. Start with the high-priority topics in this order, use the source map for detail, and keep the unused Rust lane separate.

Overview · Overview

Review order

1. 1. Entry, eligibility, emission and gating: Start with default options and getReactFunctionType; an opt-out wins before annotation/infer/all mode selection. Then follow compileFn, errors and the replacement/import boundary. 2. 1. Entry, eligibility, emission and gating: Review gating as a semantic transformation: a named declaration becomes a const initializer; top-level pre-declaration references have an explicit check. 3. 2. HIR, control flow and SSA: Review evaluation order and CFG terminals before optimization. At joins, SSA tracks definitions and incomplete phis until predecessors are available. 4. 2. HIR, control flow and SSA: Treat identifier/successor assertions and pass ordering as contracts; a local lowering change can invalidate later scope and codegen assumptions. 5. 3. Types, effects, aliases and mutable lifetimes: The pipeline infers reference effects before dead-code elimination: apparently dead instructions may still affect inference. Preserve this ordering when adding a pass. 6. 3. Types, effects, aliases and mutable lifetimes: Readonly at a use does not mean immutable forever. Audit aliases and mutable ranges together, especially joins, stores, closures and try/catch aliases. 7. 4. React rules and explicit validation limits: Distinguish input validation from output safety: hook validation rejects problematic input, while a later flattening pass prevents memoization from making hook calls conditional. 8. 4. React rules and explicit validation limits: The setState validator documents an undetected setter hidden in a container. A successful compilation is not proof that all invalid React has been detected. 9. 4. React rules and explicit validation limits: Review preserved manual memoization after scope pruning: originally memoized outputs must not silently become unmemoized under its enabled validation. 10. 5. Construct-together scopes and hook flattening: Scope variables and instruction boundaries are separate stages. Co-mutating operands join a disjoint set; alignment and scope construction turn those lifetimes into blocks. 11. 5. Construct-together scopes and hook flattening: Flattening must propagate transitively from nested scopes. Hook calls cannot disappear on a cache hit, and use must still be observed when its result is needed. 12. 6. Dependencies, conditional reads and safe invalidation: Review dependencies as executable reads. A fine-grained path accessed only conditionally cannot simply be hoisted into an unconditional cache comparison. 13. 6. Dependencies, conditional reads and safe invalidation: Inspect jumps, returns and throws: poisoned scopes mark accesses conditional. Losing that classification can introduce a new null dereference while trying to optimize. 14. 6. Dependencies, conditional reads and safe invalidation: Deep immutability allows a shorter path to conservatively over-invalidate. This is a correctness/performance tradeoff, not a promise of minimal recomputation. 15. 7. Cache comparisons, outputs and early returns: Trace slot allocation from dependencies through declarations/reassignments. A cache-hit path must load every output required after the scope. 16. 7. Cache comparisons, outputs and early returns: Computation precedes dependency/output stores. Review this with the reconciler comment about compiler cache writes and interrupted render reuse. 17. 7. Cache comparisons, outputs and early returns: Source-file-change reset is conditional on config/source availability; Babel enables it in development. Avoid treating HMR scaffolding as unconditional production output. 18. 8. Native cache boundary and compatibility runtime: Keep three layers distinct: compiler-generated slot protocol, React dispatcher/native cache and standalone compatibility implementation. The standalone cache is not evidence of identical interrupted-render behavior. 19. 8. Native cache boundary and compatibility runtime: Inspect compatibility limitations: private internals are used by diagnostic guards, and $makeReadOnly explicitly throws TODO. Peer version metadata is not a conformance test. 20. 9. ESLint and healthcheck reuse the compiler: Compare consumers explicitly: Babel transforms; ESLint reports selected errors; healthcheck aggregates events. Their panic thresholds and reporting surfaces differ. 21. 9. ESLint and healthcheck reuse the compiler: ESLint tries Hermes then Babel for TypeScript. Parse failure and nonreportable/compiler-internal errors need separate consideration from clean lint results. 22. 10. Snapshots, evaluator parity and review proof: Review representative input/output pairs by invariant. Thousands of golden files provide regression evidence, but snapshot agreement alone does not prove semantic equivalence. 23. 10. Snapshots, evaluator parity and review proof: Fixture defaults differ from production: the harness begins in compilationMode all with all_errors. Account for pragma overrides before drawing rollout conclusions. 24. 10. Snapshots, evaluator parity and review proof: No compiler test suite was executed for this presentation run. The cited CI/test configuration describes intended checks; it is not a green build result. 25. 11. Playground as a pass-inspection tool: Use the playground to inspect pass output, but do not assume its function acceptance is identical to the Babel Program selection policy. The shown playground path requires function declarations. 26. 11. Playground as a pass-inspection tool: Source persistence is browser-side: the store serializes source into localStorage and the URL hash. This code does not establish server-side project storage. 27. 12. Rust WIP is a separate review lane: Do not draw a runtime arrow from Babel compilation into Rust just because both trees contain SSA/HIR. The N-API parse entry returns serialized program/diagnostics and has its own analysis boundary.

Extension guidance

Proposed extension · 1. Entry, eligibility, emission and gating: For a new selection policy, change entrypoint options/selection and add opt-in, opt-out, anonymous-function and existing-runtime-import fixtures. Keep optimization passes independent of selection. Proposed extension · 1. Entry, eligibility, emission and gating: For a new rollout strategy, exercise named/default exports and hoisted uses through Gating and Program before changing code generation. Proposed extension · 2. HIR, control flow and SSA: For new JavaScript syntax, extend lowering plus HIR/visitors/printers and add branching/loop fixtures; do not begin with emitted text substitutions. Proposed extension · 3. Types, effects, aliases and mutable lifetimes: For a new library signature, investigate Environment/Globals/ObjectShape rather than adding ad-hoc purity assumptions in codegen; test mutation, aliases and closure capture. Proposed extension · 4. React rules and explicit validation limits: A new React rule should have explicit error severity, source locations and tests through both compiler and ESLint reporting. Verify the flag default rather than assuming all checks run. Proposed extension · 5. Construct-together scopes and hook flattening: For a scope optimization, check overlap, block nesting, hook flattening, early returns and escaping outputs before measuring cache savings. Proposed extension · 6. Dependencies, conditional reads and safe invalidation: When refining property dependencies, add optional-chain, guarded-null and break/continue/early-return fixtures, then compare behavior as well as output size. Proposed extension · 7. Cache comparisons, outputs and early returns: For new memoized outputs, change structured codegen and exercise cold cache, unchanged inputs, changed inputs, early returns and throws. Keep import insertion at the Program boundary. Proposed extension · 8. Native cache boundary and compatibility runtime: For a new runtime target, test c(size), sentinel initialization, slot-count stability, update/interrupt behavior and import selection; do not infer support solely from peerDependencies. Proposed extension · 9. ESLint and healthcheck reuse the compiler: When adding a diagnostic, run it through compiler error handling, ESLint severity/location filtering and healthcheck categorization. A pass-level unit test alone cannot establish all three surfaces. Proposed extension · 10. Snapshots, evaluator parity and review proof: For every semantic fix, add a minimal fixture and evaluator input covering unchanged and changed props, plus an expected diagnostic case where relevant. Review snapshot changes manually. Proposed extension · 11. Playground as a pass-inspection tool: For a new pass view, preserve the pipeline generator/logging contract and test the Editor output path separately from Babel integration. Proposed extension · 12. Rust WIP is a separate review lane: For Rust-port work, follow the crate-specific tests and snapshots and define the integration boundary before claiming feature parity with TypeScript.

Entry and rollout: first decide what may change · Deep dive

A Program-level compiler

Babel visits Program so compilation runs close to source before visitor merging can obscure it. The visitor parses options, adjusts Reanimated configuration and enables source-change cache reset in development. Program then owns file selection and replacement; optimization passes operate on a selected function. This separation is the first extension seam to preserve.

Entry and rollout: first decide what may change · Deep dive

Eligibility is a policy, not every function

The default mode is infer. Function-level opt-outs take precedence; opt-ins may compile an otherwise Other function. Annotation mode requires opt-in; all mode restricts compilation to top-level functions. Classes are outside the stated design goals. Review fixtures in their configured mode: the snapshot harness starts from all, not the production default.

Entry and rollout: first decide what may change · Deep dive

Gating also changes JavaScript declaration behavior

The gated output selects compiled or original function expressions. A named declaration ordinarily becomes a const initializer. This loses declaration hoisting, so Program checks top-level uses before the declaration before replacement. The review question is larger than whether the feature flag chooses the right branch: exports, binding identity and pre-declaration references must remain valid.

Failure policy and the AST boundary · Deep dive

Compilation can report without replacing

compileProgram calls compileFn inside error handling, logs success metadata and queues replacements only when noEmit is false and the current critical-error state allows it. Error severity and panicThreshold determine whether processing throws. Invalid configuration always throws. Follow this path when a function appears unchanged rather than assuming the optimizer found nothing useful.

Failure policy and the AST boundary · Deep dive

Replacement and imports are a final boundary

Program builds replacement function nodes, inserts gated or direct versions, and asks for a memo-cache import only if compiled functions used memo slots. The memo-cache module defaults to react/compiler-runtime and is configurable. Extension work should retain this boundary instead of having individual optimization passes mutate module imports.

Lowering and SSA: make semantics explicit · Deep dive

Preserve source structure while exposing control flow

HIR is deliberately high-level: it retains distinctions such as logical expressions versus conditionals and different loop forms while representing basic blocks and terminals. Lowering resolves bindings and turns patterns into explicit operations. Review observable evaluation order here before inspecting how many memoized blocks are emitted; a faster wrong evaluation order is still a compiler bug.

Lowering and SSA: make semantics explicit · Deep dive

Joins and loop back edges require explicit definitions

SSA tracks the current definition per block. When not all predecessors are available, it creates incomplete phis; multiple predecessors may need a phi. It records a definition before recursively following loop edges to terminate recursion. This explains why a seemingly local variable transformation can affect inference far from the original statement.

Lowering and SSA: make semantics explicit · Deep dive

Pass order is an architectural dependency

The pipeline checks identifier consistency and terminal successors around normalization/SSA, eliminates redundant phis and propagates constants before type inference. These calls are the authoritative execution order at the pinned revision; prose design notes are orientation. When inserting a pass, write down which IR invariants it requires and preserves.

Inference: values, references and lifetimes · Deep dive

Types support optimization without trusting annotations by default

inferTypes generates equations, unifies them and applies resolved types to phis, lvalues, operands and nested functions. The Environment defaults do not trust user type annotations. These are conservative categories useful to analysis, including hooks and primitives, rather than a replacement for a complete TypeScript type checker.

Inference: values, references and lifetimes · Deep dive

A readonly reference can still point to mutable data

Reference effects describe a particular use: readonly means that use does not modify a value, while later uses may. Frozen values rely on React ownership/immutability assumptions. Aliasing carries these facts across assignments. Review props, hook arguments/returns, JSX capture and closures with those assumptions visible; do not translate every readonly use into permanent purity.

Inference: values, references and lifetimes · Deep dive

Do not delete an inference witness too early

Reference effects run before dead-code elimination because dead instructions may still affect inference. Mutable-range inference then refines aliases through stores and phis until the canonical alias map stabilizes, followed by lifetime reinference. Changing the sequence can change which values are considered to construct together.

React rules: guarantees and blind spots · Deep dive

Two defenses protect hook semantics

Input hook validation classifies known and potential hooks and checks unconditional calling. Later scope flattening removes memoization around scopes transitively containing hooks or use. The two defenses answer different questions: whether the input is acceptable, and whether cache-hit output would skip a required call.

React rules: guarantees and blind spots · Deep dive

Configuration changes the validation surface

Hooks and unconditional setState validation default on; render-time ref access and memoized effect dependency validation default off. Capitalized-call validation defaults to null. A review should name the active configuration. A passing compiler run does not mean every available validator was enabled.

React rules: guarantees and blind spots · Deep dive

Known false negatives and manual memoization matter

The setState validator explicitly documents a setter hidden in an array as an undetected case. Separately, late preserved-manual-memoization validation checks that originally memoized values did not become unmemoized after scope transformations. Treat these as specific checks with limits, not proof that all Rules of React or referential-equality expectations are satisfied.

Reactive scopes: values that must construct together · Deep dive

Group mutation before choosing statement boundaries

The first scope pass groups mutable operands with disjoint sets and assigns scope identities/ranges. It explicitly does not determine every instruction needed to compute the group. Alignment, overlap merging and scope-block construction follow; at this revision a flag selects HIR scope handling or the older ReactiveFunction path.

Reactive scopes: values that must construct together · Deep dive

A cache hit may not erase a hook call

Most scope inference is hook-agnostic. The later flattening pass visits nested scopes and propagates hasHook outward, replacing an affected scope with its instructions. This can discard an attractive memoization opportunity, but it preserves required hook/use participation. Review nested cases, not only a single top-level hook.

Reactive scopes: values that must construct together · Deep dive

Pruning is part of correctness and cost control

After dependency propagation the pipeline prunes nonescaping, nonreactive and unused work, merges scopes that invalidate together, prunes always-invalidating scopes and propagates early returns. More scopes do not automatically mean better output: cache comparisons and extra code have costs and the goals explicitly reject perfect minimal recomputation.

Dependencies are executable code · Deep dive

Propagate from children to parents

A scope depends on non-stable values created before its start; parent dependencies include child dependencies. Temporaries used outside their defining scope are tracked so output and dependency analysis agree. Follow this pass when a nested operation unexpectedly broadens a memoization boundary.

Evidence (1 reference)
compiler/packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler/src/ReactiveScopes/PropagateScopeDependencies.ts:42–74
Dependencies are executable code · Deep dive

Do not hoist a conditional property read

The minimal dependency tree preserves all dependencies while ensuring final comparisons can read them unconditionally. If props.user.name was only accessed after a guard, checking that deep path before the guard may throw. A safe parent path can conservatively invalidate more often. Deep immutability justifies that broader check; it does not make every deep read safe.

Dependencies are executable code · Deep dive

Jumps change which accesses are unconditional

The propagation pass marks scopes poisoned by relevant jump targets or outermost throws/returns, making dependencies conditional. Add break, continue, early-return and optional-chain examples when modifying this logic. A source diff showing fewer dependency slots is not sufficient evidence of a safe improvement.

From scopes to cache branches · Deep dive

Allocate slots for inputs and outputs

Codegen assigns a slot per dependency and compares it with !==. It also allocates slots for scope declarations and reassignments, creates stores and restores named outputs on the hit path. Review both sides of the branch: correctly detecting unchanged inputs is useless if an escaping result is not reloaded.

From scopes to cache branches · Deep dive

Cold cache and successful computation define the write boundary

With dependencies, comparison expressions are ORed. Without dependencies, codegen checks the first output slot against Symbol.for(react.memo_cache_sentinel). It emits the computation before appending stores; the alternative loads cached outputs. Compare this with the reconciler comment about atomic input/output cache writes when reviewing throws or interrupted renders.

From scopes to cache branches · Deep dive

Early returns and development reset use extra protocols

An early-return value is checked against its own sentinel before returning outside a memoized block. Development source-change reset may reserve another cache slot and reset stored values when the source hash changes. These are structured control-flow/runtime contracts, so a codegen extension must exercise more than the ordinary return-at-end example.

Runtime compatibility is a boundary, not a label · Deep dive

Default output reaches the existing React dispatcher

react/compiler-runtime re-exports useMemoCache as c. ReactHooks delegates to the current dispatcher; the reconciler locates or allocates the per-render memo cache, initializes sentinel slots and checks stable size in development. These unchanged contextual files explain where new compiler output fits the surrounding React runtime.

Runtime compatibility is a boundary, not a label · Deep dive

Native cache behavior and the standalone package differ

The reconciler contains explicit clone/share behavior controlled by enableNoCloningMemoCache and discusses interrupted updates. The standalone package instead returns a useState-initialized array. Both use the sentinel protocol, but the source shown does not prove identical concurrency or interruption semantics. runtimeModule selects the import source.

Runtime compatibility is a boundary, not a label · Deep dive

Read optional diagnostics and incomplete exports literally

The standalone package uses private React internals for optional dispatcher guards. Its $read rejects a sentinel read and $reset restores sentinels; $makeReadOnly throws TODO. Peer dependencies list React versions, but that metadata cannot establish feature completeness. A runtime extension needs behavior tests at the target boundary.

One compiler, different developer surfaces · Deep dive

ESLint requests analysis and selects diagnostics

The rule uses noEmit, infer mode and all_errors. It parses with Hermes, falls back to Babel for TypeScript, runs the compiler plugin and reports selected located diagnostics. It is a consumer of compiler errors, not a separate React rule engine that guarantees all internal compiler failures are visible to users.

One compiler, different developer surfaces · Deep dive

Healthcheck counts compiler events

Healthcheck also uses noEmit but chooses critical_errors and a logger. CompileSuccess contributes to success counts; InvalidReact/InvalidJS become actionable failures; other events remain distinct. Compilation coverage is useful readiness information. It does not run the optimized application or demonstrate a performance improvement.

Tests: golden output plus behavioral comparison · Deep dive

Navigate fixtures by invariant

snap dispatches discovered fixtures to workers or synchronous transforms. Workers check expected-error naming and gather generated output. Keep the input and golden output side by side for an invariant: alias lifetime, hook flattening, dependency null safety or early return. The corpus is supporting coverage, not thousands of distinct production modules.

Tests: golden output plus behavioral comparison · Deep dive

Sprout checks observable parity for supplied examples

When evaluator code exists, Sprout executes original and compiled forms and compares result kind, value and logs. Sequential renders mount once and rerender with provided props. This catches behavior that a golden text diff cannot, but only for the supplied cases; it is not exhaustive equivalence proof.

Playground, Rust and a practical review route · Deep dive

Review from invariants to evidence

Suggested order: entry/failure policy; HIR and effects; rule validation; scope/dependency safety; codegen/runtime; diagnostics and representative test pairs. Use topic filters for the semantic lane and file coverage for the full inventory. Add new syntax at lowering, library knowledge at inference/environment, a new rule in validation/consumers and a new cache protocol at codegen plus runtime.
